goal: Add an incremental batch wrapper around New-PluginZip.ps1 that rebuilds every changed plugin under plugins/ in one call.

steps.action: Write scripts/Update-PluginZips.ps1: enumerate each dir under plugins/, compare newest source-file mtime to its zip mtime, rebuild via New-PluginZip.ps1 only when stale/missing or -Force, optional -Validate runs claude plugin validate per rebuild.

Ran it for real three times: plain run (found 5 of 6 zips genuinely stale, rebuilt exactly those, left pmcro-trail alone), -Force -Validate (rebuilt all 6, all validated pass), plain run again (all 6 correctly reported up-to-date, 0 rebuilt).
Updated packaging-checklist.asset.md (new subsection under 3), references/README.md (asset map row), SKILL.md (workflow step + references) to document the new script.
Verified the incremental logic discriminates correctly in both directions (stale -> rebuilt, current -> skipped) using real timestamps on the actual plugin zips, not a synthetic/mocked test.

success_criteria: Update-PluginZips.ps1 exists, defaults to incremental, supports -Force and -Validate
It is a thin wrapper -- every rebuild goes through New-PluginZip.ps1, not a reimplementation
Real run against this repo correctly distinguished stale vs up-to-date zips (not just tested in the abstract)
Docs (checklist, README asset map, SKILL.md) all mention it
out_of_scope: Auto-uploading rebuilt zips to Cowork (no API for that available to this repo)
Watching plugins/ for changes continuously -- this is an on-demand CLI tool, not a daemon
